Email [seccoffice@worldbank.org](mailto:seccoffice@worldbank.org) **What are the dates for the Annual Meetings?** The 2026 Annual Meetings will take place from Monday, October 12 to Sunday, October 18, 2026. --- **What is the format of the Meetings?** The Annual Meetings will take place in person in Bangkok, Thailand. Some events will be streamed online. Fully accredited individuals will be able to attend meetings in person. Public events will be streamed live and available on World Bank Group and IMF digital platforms, accessible to everyone regardless of registration status. Event stream links, where applicable, will be available on the [schedule](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/schedule). --- **How can I follow events virtually?** The Annual Meetings will be in person, and public events will be streamed live and accessible online. Once the schedule is live on [AMWeb](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/schedule), attendees can click "View Event" to watch the event stream (where available). If prompted to log in, participants should enter the email address they used to register and the unique Registration ID provided in the Registration Confirmation letter. --- **Who can I contact if I am interested to be a future Speaker?** Please email your contact details along with a professional summary and your areas of expertise to SECCOffice@worldbank.org and we will direct your inquiry to the appropriate Bank team. --- **Where can I find information about IMF events?** For information about IMF events, please visit the IMF website: [https://imfconnect.org](https://imfconnect.org/). --- **How can I watch the Program of Events/Public Program?** The schedule for the public program of events is available on [AMWeb](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/schedule). The public program of events will be streamed on World Bank Live [https://live.worldbank.org](https://live.worldbank.org/). --- **Will there be taped recordings available to watch past meetings?** The public program of events will be recorded and available for replay at [https://live.worldbank.org](https://live.worldbank.org/). Any recordings of other events will be available to Bank staff and registered attendees by clicking "View Event" on the schedule, but many events are typically not available for replay. --- **Are we able to get Transcripts of the events that are listed as "Open to Registrants"?** Transcripts are not generally available for events. You may inquire with the event organizer. --- **My username or password is not working.** If you received a registration Confirmation from [MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org), make sure you are typing the registration ID/password in exactly as listed (note, if copying/pasting make sure there are no spaces at the end of the registration ID/password, and make sure your keyboard is not replacing any English characters). You can use the "password reveal" option by clicking on the eye icon to see what password you entered. Please make sure that you are using the email address you used to register for the Meetings. If you received your registration confirmation within the past hour of trying to log in, there may be a slight delay with the system recognizing credentials and it’s advised that you try again in another hour. If you have not received your registration confirmation letter, your registration has not yet been approved and you will not be able to login until you receive a registration confirmation letter. Those still experiencing issues logging in should email [SECCOffice@worldbank.org](mailto:SECCOffice@worldbank.org). --- **What should I do if I need special assistance or accommodations due to a disability?** If you have a disability and require assistance to fully participate in the Meetings, you will have the opportunity to share your needs when you register for the Meetings. If you have questions, please contact our support team at MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org. --- **How can I download the IMF | World Bank Meetings mobile app?** TheIMF | World Bank Meetings app can be downloaded from the [Apple store for iOs devices](https://apps.apple.com/hr/app/imf-world-bank-meetings/id6742815336), or [Google play for Android devices](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.imf.imfwbmeetings&pcampaignid=web_share). Bank registrants should click "Email Address & Password" on the login page, and then click "Request a Password." Enter your email address, and the app will send you a temporary code from [noreply@worldbank.org](mailto:noreply@worldbank.org). (If you did not receive the email, please check your spam or junk folders). Once you log in, you can set your own password and update your profile. If you have trouble logging in, please email [AMRegITSupport@worldbank.org](mailto:AMRegITSupport@worldbank.org). **Do I need to register? How do I register? Where can I find registration instructions?** The public program of events for the Spring and Annual Meetings are streamed on World Bank Live ([live.worldbank.org](https://live.worldbank.org/)) and are available to all persons without registering. Registration is required to attend the meetings in person, and to follow along with any by-invitation-only events that have a streaming option. Registration guidance can be found on the Annual Meetings website, [AMWeb](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/registration). --- **What are the requirements to register for the Meetings?** A description of the registration requirements can be found under each category on the Registration Page on AMWeb, . Attendees should review the requirements under each category to ensure they are applying under the correct category. Applying under the incorrect category will delay processing of your application. If you believe you have submitted your application under the wrong category, email [MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org.](mailto:MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org) --- **How long does registration confirmation take?** Confirmation time varies but can take approximately 2 to 3 weeks. You will be notified via email when your application is approved. If you have applied more than 3 weeks ago and would like an update on the status of your application, please email [MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org). Duplicate applications will not be processed and may delay processing of your registration request. --- **What is my Registration ID?** A Registration ID is a unique identifier that is provided to each registrant in the registration confirmation letter sent by [MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org). The Registration ID along with the email address used to register are required to access any virtually accessible by-invitation-only events. IMF attendees should refer to their registration confirmation email from the IMF. If you did not receive a registration confirmation email, your registration request is still being processed and you will receive an email once your registration is confirmed. --- **Is there a fee to register? Is there a fee to watch specific events?** There is **no fee** to register or watch specific events. **Do you have a list of all participants to the Meetings?** The Participant List can be found on, [AMWeb](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/schedule), by clicking on the [Networking](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/networking) tab. This list shows people who have registered with the Bank and have opted in to be shown on the list. The list will be posted beginning in mid-March and updated weekly. --- **I need to contact a speaker or participant; how can I connect?** Please visit the Annual Meetings website, [AMWeb](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/networking), then navigate to [Networking](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/networking) to find the Participants List, which is posted after registration opens. This information can also be found under the Speakers and/or Participants tab on the IMF | World Bank Meetings mobile app. The mobile app can be downloaded from the [Apple store for iOs devices](https://apps.apple.com/hr/app/imf-world-bank-meetings/id6742815336), or [Google play for Android devices](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.imf.imfwbmeetings&pcampaignid=web_share). --- **How can I get more information about the Civil Society Policy Forum?** Information about the Civil Society Policy Forum can be found on the CSO website as it becomes available: [https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/partners/civil-society/civil-society-policy-forum](https://www.worldbank.org/en/events/2022/06/16/civil-society-policy-forum-annual-meetings-2022) --- **How can I get more information about the Global Parliamentary Forum?** Please visit  for more information about the Parliamentarian Network. --- **How can media participate in any of the events?** Accredited journalists can submit a [registration request](https://www.worldbank.org/en/meetings/splash/annual/registration#sec5)to be registered to attend the Meetings. Additionally, journalists can access the IMF’s [Online Media Briefing Center](https://mediacenter.imf.org/) and the World Bank’s [Online Media Briefing Center](https://media.worldbank.org/). For further information on media access to the various press conferences and to receive broadcast materials, please contact the media relations teams at the IMF ([media@imf.org](mailto:media@imf.org)) and World Bank Group ([press@worldbank.org](mailto:press@worldbank.org)). The public program of events can be viewed on [World Bank Live](https://live.worldbank.org/). --- **What time zone are the events in?** All events are listed as local time in Bangkok, Thailand (GMT+7). --- **Why am I not appearing on the "Participant List" (either PDF version or within Meetings Login page)?** **For Bank Staff:**The Participant List shows those who have opted in when registering for the Meetings. The PDF Participant List will display only non-Bank staff who have opted in. If you would like to be shown on the Participant List in the Meetings Login page, please send an email to [MeetingsHR@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsHR@worldbank.org) and we will update your account. **For other participants:**The Participant List shows those who have opted in when registering for the Meetings. If you would like to be shown on the Participant List, your registration record will need to be updated. Please send an email to [MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org) and we will update your account. --- **How do I send messages to other participants?** Once you have accessed the Meetings Login Page, you will see a tab called "Participants" and a tab called "Inbox" at the top of the page. "Inbox" will show any messages that you have received, and you can also send a message from this page. You can also go to the "Participants" tab and view the list of attendees who have opted in to be shown on this listing and click "Send Message" next to a name to send a message to that person. This information can also be found under the Speakers and/or Participants tab on the IMF | World Bank Meetings mobile app. The mobile app can be downloaded from the [Apple store for iOs devices](https://apps.apple.com/hr/app/imf-world-bank-meetings/id6742815336), or [Google play for Android devices](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.imf.imfwbmeetings&pcampaignid=web_share). Users who have signed in and opted in to receive messages will be able to send direct messages to other participants within the app. --- **How do I stop receiving messages from other participants? / How do I remove my name from the Participant list?** **For Bank Staff**: Please email [MeetingsHR@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsHR@worldbank.org) with your request to be removed from the Participant List, which will also mean you will no longer have access to the messaging feature. **For other participants**: To be removed from the Participant List and to be removed from the messaging function, your registration record will need to be updated. Please send an email to [MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org](mailto:MeetingsRegistration@worldbank.org) and we will update your account. snippet: Established in 1944 as a part of the United Nations system, the IMF's primary purpose is to ensure the stability of the international monetary system—the system of exchange rates and international payments that enables countries and their citizens to buy goods and services from each other. This is essential for sustainable economic growth and rising living standards. To maintain stability and prevent crises in the international monetary system, the IMF conducts surveillance of national, regional, and global economic and financial developments. It provides advice to its 190 member countries, encouraging them to adopt policies that foster economic stability, reduce their vulnerability to economic and financial crises, and raise living standards. The IMF also serves as a forum where its global membership can discuss the national, regional, and global consequences of their policies. The IMF makes financing temporarily available to member countries to help them address balance of payments problems—that is, when they find themselves short of foreign exchange to meet their payments to other countries. Finally, the IMF provides countries with training to help them build the expertise and institutions they need for economic stability and growth.

snippet: The IMF has a management team and 17 departments that carry out its country, policy, analytical, and technical work. One department is charged with managing the IMF's resources. The Managing Director is assisted by a First Deputy Managing Director and three other Deputy Managing Directors. The IMF's employees come from all over the world; they are responsible to the IMF and not to the authorities of the countries of which they are citizens. The IMF staff is organized mainly into area; functional; and information, liaison, and support responsibilities. The IMF's Finances page provides a wealth of information and financial data representing members relations with the IMF. The IMF's resources come mainly from the money that countries pay as their capital subscription when they become members.
